title: Thoughts on Nicolas Winding Refns films

commenti.body: NWR is one of my favorite directors, his unique audio/visual style makes his films standout. I would  recommend his mini series Too Old to Die Young if you enjoy his work. He claims the episodes can be watched in any order.
Pusher I & II are amongst the best crime films of all time, particularly II. The vicious cycle of crime and the inability to escape this lifestyle are themes that always elevate the genre.

He's one of my favourite working directors right now. I love his brand of "empty, pornographic" (his words) thrillers where the style very much IS the substance. He's distinct from the other 70s worshipping minimal arty guys - like you mentioned, his films as audio experiences really help him there. And a lot about his visuals came into focus when I learned he is colour blind. Too Old To Die Young and Copenhagen Cowboy were two of the coolest, most striking and memorable shows I've watched in recent years. And the former didn't even have an ending, they just ran out of money!

Having just sucked his dick a whole bunch, I'd be remiss not to say that I totally understand why someone could find his output entirely without nourishment as arthouse or genre fare; some people hate his musical tastes, the way he directs actors, the sleepy pacing, the clipped performances and long pauses. I've seen most of his endings criticised specifically. You aren't watching him for the writing or the big ideas being churned over; he's more of an overall sustained effect kind of guy, his films immediately wash over you in a really enjoyable way if you connect with them.

(Also a few of my gay mates really love him and are forever holding court about his straight-but-very-gay and objectifying eye for the male form. It's interesting stuff to consider, a neat wrinkle for a director who is mostly seen as creating vacuous machismo bullshit. One mate, the last time we were drinking and chatting shit about films, made the observation that Refn is to the male body what David Lynch is for the female. Interesting.)

OP, you might enjoy [this series of interviews](https://youtu.be/hGfu6AGkgHY?si=KytooHh2a5GwCdp8) with NWR, made back in 2007. They are from before any of the films you mentioned and after the Pusher trilogy (which you should also watch, if you haven't already). It's in Danish, but subtitled. He's such a strange character, and the interviews reflect that - in a good way.

His style is impressive and I truly appreciate his commitment to film restoration and preservation but I don't think he has anything interesting to say as an artist other than creating an antagonistic relationship with his audience and critics by maximizing fairly unoriginal genre tropes. Overall I'm a fan, but a mild one and can't listen to him speak for more than two minutes without wanting to puncture my eardrums. I love the clip of Friedkin insulting him to his face.
Copenhagen Cowboy was out there but I enjoyed it. The Hideo Kojima cameo at the end was fucking bizarre though.
